summary:
Verified the linkage_campuses research file: 51 sources, 122 evidence items, and 54 entities (24 companies, 6 refinements, 24 requirements). Result: 42 publish, 12 publish_flagged, 0 reject. All 122 evidence quotes were confirmed verbatim in their cited documents (whitespace/curly-quote/hyphenation differences only) using direct fetches, Wayback Machine mirrors of the exact SEC URL (for filings www.sec.gov blocked to a declared, non-browser-disguised User-Agent), or EDGAR full-text search phrase-matching scoped to the filer's CIK and cross-checked against the cited accession number when a filing was too large or otherwise unreachable by direct fetch (SB Energy's S-1/A, WEC's and X-Energy's 10-Qs, and one Oracle 8-K). No quote was found to be fabricated, paraphrased, or missing.

Systemic/analyst-specific findings:
1. Foxconn Houston / Wistron Fort Worth (4 refinements): publish_flagged. Each site claim is independently well-supported by NVIDIA's own Tier 2 releases naming the plant and product, but each refines a flow whose only other evidentiary basis is NVIDIA's 10-K boilerplate listing Hon Hai/Wistron/Fabrinet collectively without naming any site. Flagged so the map doesn't read as if 100% of each company's NVIDIA assembly work is concentrated at that one plant.
2. Colossus II electricity (co:xai as sole supplier): publish_flagged. The S-1/A's "self-built behind-the-meter" language is accurate and verified, but listing the operator itself as "supplier" documents self-generation, not a third-party dependency; flagged so the single-point-of-failure reading isn't misread as naming an external vendor.
3. Prometheus (Sidecat = Prometheus): publish_flagged, statement corrected. The identification rests on matching city and Meta parentage across two separate documents, not one document naming both; disclosed as inference in the corrected statement.
4. Denton AI hardware: publish_flagged, statement corrected. Core Scientific's language is hedged ("we believe this addition aligns with... NVIDIA GPU operations") and never confirms NVIDIA hardware at the site; corrected to reflect that.
5. Eleven/twelve new utility companies: all verified and published; five (Lancium, DTE Energy, Will-Power OH, AEP, Murphy Electric Power Board) flagged only because their hq coordinates approximate a project/service region rather than a documented corporate address (self-disclosed in the record's own address field) — not a factual error.
6. Susquehanna -> AWS Salem Township and Longhorn turbines -> Abilene campus (via Abilene DC 1, LLC): both publish without flags. The Abilene chain is unusually solid — the identical legal entity name ("Abilene DC 1, LLC") appears independently in the TCEQ permit and the Blue Owl SEC exhibit, which is close to direct documentation despite the underlying flow being marked "inferred" upstream. The Susquehanna chain is corroborated by Talen's own glossary defining the "AWS Data Campus" term plus the PA Governor's release naming Salem Township for Amazon's AI campuses.
7. Minor, non-blocking note: three requirements (req:ports-pike-electricity, req:stargate-milam-electricity) list PJM and ERCOT as "suppliers" of electricity when they are actually grid/market operators, not generators; the underlying statement text already correctly describes their real roles (transmission/interconnection), so no correction was needed, but this is a recurring category looseness worth tightening in future rounds.

No entity was rejected: every requirement and refinement had at least one verified Tier 1/2 item supporting its material claims, and the SPOF-sensitive single-supplier requirements (Denton, Dalton, Marble, Muskogee, Saline, Madison County, Colossus/Colossus II, Fairwater Wisconsin, PORTS-Pike hardware) all had evidence using explicit sole-supplier/dependency language ("100% of the power," "dependent on NVIDIA for... the necessary GPU units," "a single... cluster") sufficient to meet the publish bar, except Denton and Prometheus as flagged above. Prose audit (2026-10-01): removed four statement figures not found in any cited quote.
